summary: MintLance concurrent session stall causing truncated completions and temporary invoice/billing delta during us-east peak
description:
Issue summary:
During a sustained traffic peak on 2026-03-10 09:02-09:46 UTC MintLance experienced high rates of truncated responses (clients reported streaming connections closing mid-completion) and a subsequent unexpected billing delta attributed to duplicate acknowledgement accounting.

Impact:
- ~12% of requests from MintLance in us-east experienced truncated streaming completions (partial transcripts).
- Brief billing spike visible on customer's invoice preview window for the affected timeframe (~$480 extra before automated credit).
- Customer-facing producers reported degraded UX for chat features during morning traffic peak; no data exfiltration identified.

Environment:
- Redwood prod cluster in us-east serving MintLance dedicated pool (dedicated capacity, pool-id dl-mintlance-1).
- Models routed to rw/opt-6.7b-quantized-v2 with streaming enabled.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) High concurrency from MintLance runtime jobs starting at ~09:02 UTC.
2) KV prefix cache miss flood (many new conversation prefixes) increased per-request setup cost.
3) Serving runtime started shedding long-lived streaming connections under backpressure; some connections closed with 499/stream-reset.
4) Client retries combined with router-level partial-ack duplication produced duplicate billing events for a subset of short-lived retries.

Logs / evidence pointers:
- SRE dashboard: links to request-rate, tail latency, and streaming-reset graphs in Grafana (see related_confluence_pages).
- Example streaming trace: request-id 1a7b2f4d showing abrupt grpc stream close at 09:12:18 UTC (attached to internal trace).
- Billing ledger row samples in BigQuery: project redwood-billing.mintlance_tmp.billing_events_20260310 showing duplicate ack events for request-id hash range xxxxx..yyyyy.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: concurrent KV cache miss and a rare router backpressure path combined to close streaming connections without completing token accounting.

Timestamps and findings:
- 09:02 UTC: MintLance concurrent job window begins (customer reported a scheduled batch of user sessions).
- 09:07-09:20 UTC: KV cache miss rate spiked to 1400% of baseline for the dedicated pool; eviction churn increased CPU on serving nodes.
- 09:10 UTC: Router ingress observed queue growth; router began responding with RESET_STREAM to long-lived streams when per-node inflight tokens exceeded safety threshold.
- 09:12 UTC: Several clients retried immediately; retry logic created short-lived requests that completed quickly and created duplicate ack entries in billing pipeline due to idempotency gap for streaming-early-terminations.

Hypotheses validated by logs:
- We found router logs showing explicit RESET_STREAM events correlated with the same request-ids as truncated traces.
- Billing pipeline consumer acknowledged events twice when stream token accounting did not include retry-de-dup metadata (race between ack persistence and retry dedup token write).

Temporary mitigations applied during incident:
1) Increased per-router streaming inflight safety threshold for dl-mintlance-1 by 25% to reduce premature resets.
2) Applied a KV cache TTL bump and warmed common prefixes via a preheat job to reduce miss churn.
3) Issued a manual billing credit to MintLance while investigation proceeded.

Open risks noted:
- Similar mis-specified client retry windows could retrigger duplicate ack behavior unless idempotency tokens are enforced end-to-end.

resolution:
Root cause: a combination of KV cache miss storm causing serving node CPU pressure and a router safety path that reset long-lived streams when inflight tokens exceeded threshold. Client retry behavior plus a small idempotency gap in the billing ingestion pipeline produced duplicate ack/billing events.

Fixes implemented:
- Short-term: increased router threshold and warmed KV prefixes during the incident window; issued customer credit.
- Medium-term: patched billing ingestion to validate idempotency tokens on early-terminated streams (PR merged and deployed 2026-03-12).
- Long-term: engineering backlog items added to: (1) improve backpressure flow to allow graceful drain rather than immediate RESET_STREAM; (2) enhance KV warm-up heuristics for dedicated pools during scheduled batch windows; (3) publish SDK retry guidance and recommended backoff windows for customers.

Follow-ups / action items (owners and ETA):
- ENG-OPS: implement graceful stream-drain flow in router (owner: Ethan Cole, ETA: 2026-04-05).
- PLAT-DEV: KV preheat/runbook for scheduled batch windows (owner: S. Navarro, ETA: 2026-03-28).
- DX/Docs: SDK retry guidance and example configs for dedicated customers (owner: Lena Ortiz, ETA: 2026-03-20).
- FINANCE: reconcile credit in next billing run and confirm final adjustment (owner: M. Deng, ETA: 2026-03-20).

Status: Incident resolved; customer satisfied with remediation and credit. Postmortem published at related_confluence_pages.
